memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But Esau ran to meet Jacob and embraced him; he threw his arms around his neck and kissed him. And they wept." - Gen 33:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is one of the most moving verses in Genesis. Jacob had braced himself for anger, perhaps even for death. Instead, "Esau ran to meet Jacob and embraced him; he threw his arms around his neck and kissed him. And they wept." All the fear, all the dread of this reunion, melts in a flood of tears and forgiveness. The brother who once vowed to kill Jacob now runs to embrace him.

What happened? God had gone before Jacob and softened Esau's heart. Jacob had prayed, "Save me from the hand of my brother" (Gen 32:11), and God answered — not with a battle won, but with a heart changed. The reconciliation Jacob could never have forced, God graciously gave.

There is something here that should stir our hearts, for these very words echo forward. Centuries later, Jesus would describe a father who saw his lost son returning and "ran to his son, threw his arms around him and kissed him" (Luke 15:20). Esau's welcome of Jacob is a beautiful picture of the grace God shows to returning sinners — running to embrace, not to condemn.

If you are dreading a reconciliation, remember: God can soften hearts you cannot reach. And if you are wondering whether God would welcome you back, look at that running embrace. Our God runs to receive those who return to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do I need God to soften a heart I cannot reach?
2. Do I believe God runs to welcome me when I return to Him?
3. Am I willing to offer, or receive, an embrace of grace?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You soften hearts and grant reconciliation we could never force. Thank You that You run to welcome returning sinners. Help me to give and receive grace. Amen.
